description: Every app notification now shows the app logo silhouette in the status bar instead of an unrelated function icon - background workers such as scheduled operations, network-resource sync and duplicate search no longer display the music note used by the audio player.

name: Live contact name and photo on pinned cells
description: A pinned contact cell now shows the person's current name and photo from the address book instead of what was saved when the cell was pinned, so renaming someone in the system contacts updates their cell on its own. The app explains why and asks for the contacts permission at the moment a person is pinned; refusing still pins the cell, which keeps working from the details saved at pin time. The stored snapshot also stands in when a contact is deleted or cannot be read.

name: Offline-aware stream failure
description: When a stream stops because the device itself lost its connection, the failure dialog says so and does not offer to remove the channel, and the channel keeps its amber "not confirmed" mark instead of turning red. Removal is still offered, and the red mark still applied, when the link was up and the channel itself did not respond.

name: Clock and device indicators on the launcher top bar
description: Launcher can move the clock with seconds to the left of the freed top status bar and the device indicators to the right, hiding the Start-panel tray and giving its width to a longer recent-apps list.

name: Titled sections on the launcher desktop
description: A fresh launcher desktop now opens with a titled section: App functions sits at the very top and holds the four launcher actions, and a second header below it titles everything else. A section owns the rows under its own title down to the next one, and tapping a title folds those rows away and lifts what is below - without moving a single cell, so unfolding puts every icon back on its own square. A folded title says so on screen: a chevron beside the caption turns to the folded angle, the same indicator every other collapsible section in the app uses, so a folded section is never mistaken for one that is simply empty. Folded state is kept separately for portrait and landscape and survives a rotation or a restart. A screen reader reads a title as a heading and says whether it is folded; a title offers no long-press menu, because it has none. A multi-row gadget is refused on a title row, and a header removed while arranging the desktop can be put back through the same picker every other cell comes from. An already arranged desktop is left as it is - the sections appear on a fresh or reset one.

name: Stream shortcut starts background playback without opening the Streams screen
description: Tapping a pinned radio-stream shortcut or a launcher stream tile starts the channel through the background audio service with no screen shown - feedback is the ordinary media notification, and tapping the same shortcut again stops the station. The Streams screen opens as before when background audio is switched off, when the channel is a video stream, or when there is no network. Shortcuts pinned before the update are rewritten automatically on the next app start.

name: Dialog lifecycle binding
description: Dialogs raised outside the settings helpers now close themselves when their host is destroyed, and a ratchet gate keeps new ones bound

name: Manual shooting mode is named
description: When exposure or white balance is moved off automatic while shooting the plain profile, the camera names the mode Manual instead of Normal - on the shooting profile button where the device offers a choice of profiles, and on the camera settings button where it does not.

name: Wear OS SFTP connection test
description: The Test connection button on the watch now really connects to an SFTP source, checks that its base path is reachable and reports the server's own reason on failure, instead of always answering that testing is unavailable.

name: Edit a channel from the desktop
description: Long-pressing a channel tile on the launcher desktop now offers Edit, opening the very same dialog the streams screen uses - url, title, media-kind override and the per-channel audio/subtitle preference - instead of leaving the row out because that dialog lived inside the streams screen.

name: Themed launcher icon
description: On Android 13 and newer, turning on themed icons now recolours the app icon to match the wallpaper like the system apps, instead of leaving it in full colour. Below Android 13 the icon is unchanged.

name: Background transfer progress on every screen
description: A hairline bar at the very bottom of the screen now shows a file transfer that was sent to the background, so its progress stays visible after leaving the browse screen it was started from - previously it was visible only there, or in the notification. The browse screen keeps its existing text strip instead, with the percent in figures and a tap that brings the dialog back.

name: Launch a chosen app from an edge gesture
description: The 'launch an app' gesture action now opens an app you pick, chosen separately for each of the twelve edge slots. The row under the direction names the chosen app and clears it in one tap; with no app chosen, or when the chosen app is gone, the gesture opens FastMediaSorter as before.

name: Network Monitor
description: An opt-in diagnostic program shows the current connection, signal and network details; its tests start only on user action, and its optional GNSS track remains on the device until the user shares the file.

name: Profile-aware launcher starter set
description: On first run, the launcher seeds a desktop matched to the detected device profile and adds third-party app cells only when their packages are installed.

name: Search the web from the desktop
description: A search field sits on the launcher desktop as an ordinary gadget - place it, move it, resize it or remove it like any other. Type a query, press the search key, and the result page opens in the browser; it is seeded into the starter desktop of every device profile. Nothing typed is stored on the home screen, and a device with no browser says so instead of doing nothing.

name: Place shortcuts on the home screen
description: A place shared from a map application becomes a home-screen cell that opens turn-by-turn navigation from the current position, ready to start driving. A shared short link is resolved to its coordinates while the cell is created, so tapping it needs no network; a link that cannot be resolved still becomes a cell that shows the place. The Share-sheet entry appears only while Launcher Mode is on.

name: Current-position map gadget
description: A home-screen cell drawing the current position on keyless OpenStreetMap tiles, captioned with the town and country or the coordinates, opening the system map application on tap. The place name is looked up for the centre of the map tile the cell already downloads, never for the exact position, so the address lookup publishes nothing the tile fetch has not. Tiles are cached on disk; without a location permission or a network it keeps the last known picture with a note instead of blanking.

name: Truthful file counts and a self-explaining empty folder
description: The file count on a resource card is derived from the same filter the Browse list uses, so a card can no longer promise files the list will not show. When the list is empty because the maximum file size setting removed everything, Browse names the setting and the number of hidden files instead of stating the folder was checked and holds nothing.

name: Camera bring-up off the main thread
description: Camera open no longer reads the vendor extension configuration from disk on the main thread: the lens/mode pair the first bind needs is warmed on a background dispatcher before binding, so the viewfinder comes up without the UI thread stalling

name: Grouped default desktop on first run
description: The launcher desktop a phone gets on first run opens with the content section - clock, search, weather and the media resource shortcuts - while the launcher's own actions close the desktop under their own header. Cells are packed inside their section instead of backfilling the row above it, shortcut captions sit on a translucent plate so they read over the branded wallpaper, and the weather, altitude and satellite tiles show their names before any reading arrives.

name: Pinned shortcuts survive a launcher reset
description: Shortcuts that other applications pinned to the launcher desktop come back on their own after Reset launcher settings, instead of having to be pinned again from each application. The desktop seed reads the set the system still records for this launcher and lays those cells out after the starter set, in both orientations; a shortcut whose application was removed or which its publisher stopped offering is left out, so nothing dead lands on the fresh desktop.

name: Interface in thirteen languages
description: The interface reads in thirteen languages, not three. English, Russian and Ukrainian are complete; Arabic, Bengali, Chinese (Simplified), French, German, Hindi, Italian, Portuguese, Spanish and Urdu now carry roughly 98 percent of the app's text, including the flavor-specific screens. A caption that has no translation yet falls back to English instead of appearing blank, so no screen is ever half-empty, and the system per-app language picker offers every one of the thirteen.

name: Single-eye Cast for stereo video
description: Casting a stereo 3D video to a Chromecast while the single-eye panel option is on now sends one eye only, cropped to match what the phone panel shows, instead of both half-frames side by side. The clip is prepared before the Cast session starts, so playback begins after a short wait; clips longer than the transcode ceiling are cast whole with both eyes, and live streams are never cropped.

name: Steps permission row only where the build can hold it
description: The permissions screen no longer lists the physical-activity row in builds whose manifest does not declare that permission, so the store build stops offering a grant it cannot complete; the row is gated on the same condition that puts the declaration in the manifest.

name: Edge swipe restores the command panel in fullscreen
description: In the standalone viewers, swiping the system bars back while in fullscreen now leaves fullscreen and restores the command panel; previously only the on-screen exit button did this.

name: Subtitle font styling in the panel player
description: Panel player applies the subtitle font size and family from settings; the styling call was gated behind a session flag nothing could set

name: Glide built off the main thread at startup
description: The first thumbnail grid no longer stalls: Glide is built on a background thread at startup instead of on the main thread during the first image load

name: Reuse of a recent unreachable-SFTP failure
description: An unreachable SFTP host now fails fast for a short cooldown instead of paying a full connect timeout on every stacked call of the same open

name: In-headset immersive browser
description: Inside the headset the resource opens as a 3D grid of cells rendered in the immersive scene, so files can be browsed without leaving VR for the flat panel.

name: Ray navigation in the immersive browser
description: The controller ray points at a cell in the immersive grid to select it and to enter a folder, so navigation stays in the headset.

name: Playback launch from the immersive browser
description: Choosing a file in the immersive grid starts its playback in the immersive scene directly, without a return trip through the flat browser.

name: Google account binding stable across updates
description: The bound Google account survives an app update: its stored JSON field names are pinned, so a new R8 mapping can no longer unbind it silently

name: Landscape-safe settings search button
description: Settings search button in landscape no longer falls under the system navigation bar, so it opens the search overlay instead of dismissing Settings

name: File attribute flags stable across updates
description: Hidden and read-only file flags survive an app update: the cached file list keeps them instead of silently reverting every file to default attributes

name: Stored enum values stable across updates
description: Cached file types, transfer operations and watch commands survive an app update: the enum names they store are pinned instead of being renamed by a new build mapping

name: Clean teardown after an immersive playback error
description: A failed playback in the headset now tears down cleanly: the video surface is switched off, the HUD stops mirroring a dead player and the next start no longer touches a released instance

name: No blocking preferences read during startup injection
description: Cold start no longer stalls a quarter of a second on the main thread: the file-transfer preferences open on first use instead of while the main screen is being built

name: Resource-type tabs always fit the screen
description: The resource-type filter strip sizes each tab as a share of the available width instead of a fixed width, so every tab - including Cloud - stays visible and tappable without scrolling, in portrait, landscape and on wide layouts.

name: Reflection-free timestamp storage
description: Timestamps stored by the app no longer depend on reading private fields of a platform class, a path the runtime is allowed to refuse without warning

name: Transfer result stable across updates
description: A finished file transfer is still reported correctly after an app update, and a corrupted record is discarded instead of throwing while it is read

name: Compact section header on the launcher desktop
description: A section header on the launcher desktop occupies two grid cells by one instead of a whole row, so the section's own shortcuts start in the same row immediately after it. Collapsing a section hides the cells sharing the header's row along with the rows below it, and stored positions are never rewritten. Desktops arranged by an earlier build have their headers narrowed on the next start without moving a shortcut.

name: Taskbar at the top or the bottom edge
description: Choose which edge the launcher taskbar is anchored to. The Start button, the recent and pinned app strips and the tray move together as one bar, the desktop takes the remaining safe area, and the Start menu opens from the bar's own edge. Bottom stays the default for every device profile except the car head unit, which defaults to top.

name: Viewfinder aspect selection
description: Choosing 4:3, 16:9 or full screen changes the live viewfinder stream and the saved photo, instead of drawing a result frame over a preview that was always 4:3. The choice is remembered across launches and defaults to 16:9.

name: Per-lens capture set memory
description: Every camera lens remembers its own capture set - profile, white balance, manual ISO and shutter, exposure compensation - and restores it when the user returns to that lens. The memory survives an app restart and drops any lens the device no longer enumerates.

name: Send-to for cloud and direct web files
description: Send to.. downloads a cloud or direct http(s) file into a local copy first, with percent progress, so any receiving app gets a real file; streaming manifests stay unsupported.

name: Command bar overflows into the three-dots menu
description: Main-screen command bar drops its labels before it drops commands, evicts only as many as the width shortfall requires, and offers every evicted command in the three-dots menu instead of clipping it at the screen edge.

name: Rear-lens pills when the lens has no zoom range
description: On a rear lens whose own zoom range is a single point - typically the ultra-wide - the camera shows one pill per rear lens in equivalent values (0.5 / 1 / 3) and a tap switches the optics, instead of hiding the whole zoom row and stranding the user on that lens.

name: Watch player controls, paging and screen-off mode
description: The watch players now fit a round screen and keep every control reachable: playback and file paging sit in scrolling rows that are never clipped, Favorite and screen-off share the secondary row, the rotating bezel seeks inside the current file, a track without a cover gets the brand waves-and-particles background while one with a cover shows it full-bleed, and screen-off blanks the display without stopping playback.

name: Round-safe layout on every Wear screen
description: Every Wear OS screen composes through a shared root that keeps content inside the visible glass of a round watch, shows the clock, and puts the scroll indicator beside the content instead of over it. The inset is derived from the shape and size the platform reports - a fraction of the shorter edge on a round panel, a fixed bezel gap on a square one - so it stays correct on any watch rather than being tuned to one device.

name: Branded startup splash on phone and watch
description: Launching the app now opens on its own splash instead of a bare window: the four-arrow logo arrives in the same blue as the launcher icon, growing into place rather than fading, with the app name and the line ''..All mine, here!'' beneath it in the language of the device. The watch opens on its own splash too, showing the app icon rather than this logo - Google Play requires the watch splash to match the launcher icon (see wear.splash-app-icon). The splash lasts exactly as long as the app takes to start - if it is ready sooner, it is gone sooner.

name: Watch network browsing shows the media type you asked for
description: Opening a network source on the watch under Music now lists music, under Photos photos, and under Videos videos - it used to return everything mixed together, so paging through photos could land on a file the viewer cannot show. File types the system table does not recognise, such as .mkv or .flac over FTP and SFTP, are now recognised too and no longer vanish from the list.

name: Watch opens a network source at the folder you set
description: A network source that carries a folder path from the phone now opens on the watch at that folder, instead of listing the whole server root. Sources created on the watch itself are unaffected, and a path that no longer exists reports an error rather than looking like an empty folder.

name: The watch honours the SFTP host key you pinned on the phone
description: If you pinned an SFTP server's host key on the phone, the watch now enforces that same pin: a server presenting a different key is refused before your password is ever sent. The pin travels with the source, so there is nothing to set up on the watch, and a source without a pin connects exactly as it did before.

name: Testing an FTP connection works on the watch
description: The Test connection button now really tests FTP sources on the watch. It used to refuse every time, regardless of the server, so there was no way to tell a mistyped password from a feature that was simply missing. The test checks the folder the source is set to, and gives up after about ten seconds instead of waiting indefinitely.

name: Download album art now works on the watch
description: The Download album art switch finally does what it says: a track with no cover of its own gets one fetched from the internet, and the switch turning it off really stops that. The setting had been offered both on the watch and on the phone, on by default, while nothing acted on it. Tracks that carry their own cover are unaffected.

name: Paired-phone resource on Wear
description: The watch shows the paired phone as one read-only resource: it requests folder pages on demand, the phone applies its own visibility and permission rules before every answer, and an absent phone becomes an explicit unavailable state with Retry instead of an empty list. No phone credentials or file copies are stored on the watch.

name: Google apps section on a fresh launcher desktop
description: On a device that reports Google Play services, the first launcher desktop seed and every launcher reset add a GOOGLE section holding the installed apps from an approved list - Play Store, Chrome, Gmail, Google Search, Photos, Drive, Maps, YouTube, YouTube Music, Calendar - placed after all content and before App functions. A device without Play services gets no section and no empty header, and only installed apps are placed, so the desktop never carries a dead icon.

name: Collapsed desktop sections share a row
description: Consecutive collapsed launcher sections pack their compact headers into the free positions of one row instead of taking a row each, shortening the desktop. A header is never split across rows, a section with visible content ends the chain, and stored shortcut positions are untouched - expanding restores the original layout. The desktop stays unpacked while arranging, so a drop still lands on the square it appears to.

name: Draggable scroll thumb on the desktop
description: The scroll bar on the launcher desktop can now be grabbed and dragged, not only watched: it follows a gesture scroll and scrolls the desktop when dragged, and it appears only when the desktop is longer than one screen.

name: Long-press menu on the desktop
description: A long press on an empty desktop square opens a four-item menu: add an item, edit the desktop, wallpaper, launcher settings. Adding from it uses the same content picker as the plus button in edit mode and places the new cell on the square you pressed, so a single item no longer costs a trip through edit mode. A locked desktop still ignores the gesture.

name: Other apps notifications in the launcher top bar
description: When FastMediaSorter is the home screen, the top bar can show one icon per application that currently has notifications waiting, together with how many it has, placed after the app own signals. Tapping an icon opens that application. Their title, text and attachments are never read. Off by default and inert until the user turns it on in the launcher settings and grants notification access on the system screen.

name: Now-playing card shows cover art and opens the playing app
description: The desktop now-playing cell draws the cover the media session publishes, falls back to the playing application icon, and a tap on its body opens that application when an external session is active.

name: Offline translator cell on the desktop
description: A desktop cell that translates typed or pasted text fully offline through the bundled engine, shows the language direction, and states honestly when the language pack is still missing.

name: Media window gadgets on the desktop
description: Four media window gadgets place a resource audio, video, document or image playback directly in a launcher desktop cell.

name: Status indicators open their settings section
description: Tapping a launcher status indicator opens the Android settings section it reports on.

name: Widget placement makes room and explains a refusal
description: Adding a widget to a square that is too small now slides the cells below it down, and an impossible placement explains itself instead of failing silently.

name: Start menu names desktop editing clearly
description: The Start menu entry that opens desktop editing is now named for what it edits, so it is not confused with launcher settings beside it.

name: Watch audio player: shuffle, bezel volume and a draggable position bar
description: The watch audio player can shuffle its playback set and remembers the choice across restarts, its rotating bezel now changes the system media volume with a brief on-screen readout instead of seeking, and a draggable position bar shows where playback is and moves it.

name: Clear all downloaded channels
description: The streams list can be cleared of everything that came from the internet in one confirmed action, keeping the channels added by hand.

name: Front flashlight
description: Turns the screen itself into a lamp: opens white at full window brightness, a vertical swipe changes the brightness, a small top-left button picks and remembers another colour, the time shows in black in the top-right corner, and a single tap closes it. Only the window brightness is touched, so the device setting is unchanged after it closes. Off until enabled in settings, like the other programs.

name: Labeled launcher reset button in the System group
description: The launcher settings reset action now sits in the System group as a labeled outlined button instead of an unlabeled header icon, so its purpose is readable before pressing it.

name: Remove saved credentials no resource uses
description: The remote-sources settings section shows how many saved network passwords and keys belong to no resource any more, once they have been unused past the grace period. Removing them asks first, listing each entry by address, port and user name - never the password. The count comes from the same audit the background cleanup reports from, and it updates itself after a deletion.

name: Send watch logs to developer
description: Send the watch log to the developer from the Wear About screen: the watch hands the log to the paired phone, which stores it beside its own logs and offers both by email

name: Watch log reports in the log export
description: Log reports sent from the paired Wear OS watch are stored beside the phone's own logs and are now included in both log export paths - sharing the archive and saving it to a file - so a report stays reachable after its arrival notification is dismissed.

name: Player launch reliability
description: Player opens again on every file type; it previously crashed on every open

name: Wear OS documentation as site pages
description: Public step-by-step Wear OS scenario guides with screenshots on three locales

name: Catalog update reachable from the toolbar
description: The Streams screen now shows Update catalog in its toolbar, so downloading the channel list is no longer hidden behind an overflow menu and a snackbar that fades

name: Network source media-type step
description: A network source on the watch can be opened as photos or video, not only as music: tapping a source asks which media type to browse, offers only the types enabled in settings, and skips the question when exactly one type is enabled.

name: Automatic advance at end of track
description: A finished track on the watch opens the next file of the same set by itself, wrapping to the first file past the end, instead of stopping paused at 0:00; the shuffle order is now heard without pressing next.

name: Channel preview for every live video channel
description: The channel-preview atlas covers every video channel a capture run reaches, instead of stopping at the first 2040 and dropping the rest with a warning. A build that cannot place every tile refuses and names how many channels it would leave uncovered, and the published sheet is checked against the size limit its consumers declare.

name: Automatic advance at end of video
description: With the slideshow turned on, a finished video on the watch opens the next file of the same set by itself and wraps to the first file past the end, mirroring the phone, where a video advances only while a slideshow runs; with the slideshow off the player still stops at the end, and a set of one file never restarts.

name: Connection test for a saved network source
description: Pressing and holding a saved network source on the watch offers a connection test next to delete, so a source that stopped answering can be checked without retyping it; the check runs the same probe the add form uses and reports the same result, and it is available in the store build, where the add form is not.

name: A channel keeps its pin and history when the catalog drops it and brings it back
description: A channel you pinned keeps its pin, its place in the pinned list, its OK/FAIL play history and its desktop tile even when the published catalog stops listing it and a later update brings it back. The app now recognises a channel by its address rather than by the internal row a catalog import creates, so a channel republished over http instead of https, or with a trailing slash, or with a default port spelled out, is still the same channel to you.

name: Station logo pack covers every station with cached artwork
description: The downloadable station logo pack no longer stops at a fixed 3540-tile grid: its height follows the number of logos, so stations whose artwork was already collected but fell past the old cap now show their own logo in grid mode instead of a generic icon - 608 more logos reaching 1593 more channel addresses in the 2026-08-20 rebuild

name: Channel favourite survives a cosmetic address change
description: A favourited channel keeps its star when the catalog re-publishes it under a cosmetically different address (http vs https, trailing slash, host case, default port), and tapping the star again removes the existing entry instead of quietly adding a second one

name: Resource grid cell size
description: Sets the main window resource grid to small, medium or large cells; small fits about five resources per row and large about two, scaling on top of whatever column count the device and orientation already use.

name: Network Monitor home-screen widget
description: A resizable home-screen widget that shows one of eight network readings picked when the widget is placed - Wi-Fi signal, mobile signal, Bluetooth, satellites, traffic rate, external IP, connectivity or resource reachability. Tapping it opens the Network Monitor on the matching sub-screen.

name: Network Monitor launcher desktop tile
description: A launcher desktop cell showing the same eight network readings, with the indicator chosen when the cell is placed and stored in the cell itself. Tapping the tile opens the Network Monitor on that indicator's sub-screen.

name: Connected Bluetooth devices in the Network Monitor
description: The Bluetooth section lists what is connected right now in its own frame above the paired list, reading every profile the platform will name - headset, speaker, hearing aid and watch - instead of low-energy links alone.

name: Restart a Network Monitor chart by tapping it
description: Tapping any live chart in the Network Monitor clears its observation window and starts measuring again, so one spike stops skewing the minimum, maximum and trend for the rest of the session.

name: System information as a program, and its own screen on the watch
description: System information gains its own on/off switch and appears alongside the calculator and the Network Monitor in the programs menu, the programs panel and the launcher route picker, so the report opens without going into Settings; turning the switch off removes it from all of them at once. The watch gets its own system-information screen next to About, reporting model, Wear OS version, app version, free memory and storage, and whether a phone is connected.

name: Favourites list on the watch
description: The Favourites section of the watch home screen lists the files marked on the watch itself, follows the file-list view setting, opens a row in the matching watch player, and unmarks a file from the row. Marks made before this shipped are still listed by their file name.

name: Browse the paired phone's media by type from the watch
description: The Phone section of the watch home screen offers Video, Audio, Images, Documents and All files; each opens the paired phone's media narrowed to that kind, and tapping a file fetches it from the phone and opens it in the watch player.

name: Wear companion in the programs panel
description: The watch companion is a program like the calculator: it opens in its own window from the programs panel and the programs menu, has its own visibility switch in settings, supports open-in-a-new-window and can be removed from the panel. Builds without the watch bridge show neither the entry nor the switch.

name: Send manual stream to watch
description: A stream you added yourself can be sent to the watch from the phone stream list ('Send to watch', visible with Wear Companion on); it survives watch catalog refreshes

name: Immersive HUD settings panel
description: In-headset session settings panel on the left controller menu button: stereo layout and projection overrides, control-strip distance/size, subtitles, resume position - all session-scoped, playback uninterrupted

name: Phone Browse & Favourites
description: Wear phone browse filters by media type and displays local favourites

name: Phone Resource Browser
description: Wear OS watch can browse paired phone resources

name: Stream network channel management
description: The watch requests a wide-band network while a stream plays, releases it afterward, and explains when the current link cannot carry the stream.

name: Phone Browser Folder Title
description: Watch phone-resource browser titles the screen with the folder the user is standing in, keeping the section name at the root

name: One Wear OS settings group with a master switch
description: Everything about the watch sits in one collapsible Wear OS group on the Management tab, immediately before Additional programs. Its single checkbox switches the whole companion: the button that opens the companion window, the companion's entry in the programs menu and panel, its Quick Access Panel tile and its launcher desktop shortcut all appear and disappear together, and turning it on places the shortcut on the launcher desktop by itself. Beside the checkbox a short explanation and a link open the site page describing how to install FastMedia Wear on a watch. Builds without the watch bridge show no group at all.

name: Unified capture filenames
description: Automatically names photo, screenshot, audio, camera video, screen video, and saved video-frame outputs with a source prefix, yyMMdd_HHmmss time, and collision suffix.

name: Widget backdrop opacity
description: Draws desktop gadget cells with the chosen backdrop opacity at rest, from a fully transparent cell that shows the wallpaper through it to an opaque card; edit mode always shows the full card.

name: Network thumbnail loading
description: FTP/SFTP thumbnails on the watch now load correctly instead of always showing Unavailable

name: Readable Start button and Start panel in both themes
description: The Start button, the All-apps button and every row of the Start panel keep a measured contrast of at least 7:1 against the surface beneath them, in the light and the dark theme and under each of the six colour themes. Each colour is defined per theme instead of being one value shared by both or inherited unchecked from the Material baseline, and a build gate measures the result rather than relying on a visual check.

name: Dismiss notifications from the Active signals panel
description: The Active signals panel lists each signal on one line in a two-column grid (four in landscape). A row standing for another application's notifications carries a dismiss button, and the panel header offers Dismiss all, which clears every foreign notification while leaving the app's own playback, transfer and background-work signals untouched. Signals that are not notifications carry no dismiss button at all.

name: Open a file from a phone virtual resource on the watch
description: Tapping a file listed under a phone virtual resource - camera photos, all images, all video - now opens it on the watch. The listing carries each item's MediaStore identity and the phone resolves the tap by that identity instead of by a path the virtual resource never had. A file the phone can no longer find is reported as not found, with a prompt to go back and refresh, rather than as an unreachable phone.

name: Stream home-screen widget
description: Add a stream tile straight from the Android home screen: long-press, add widget, pick the app's Stream tile, then find a channel by search with radio and video separated. One tap opens that channel.

name: Icon density chosen at launcher reset
description: Resetting the launcher desktop now asks how densely to lay the icons out, opening on the density your device profile suggests, and the starter Widgets group is filled from that profile - a photo frame gets an image window, an e-book reader a document window, a VR headset a battery tile.

name: Channel catalog loads itself when a device profile enables Streams
description: When the first-run device profile switches Streams on, the welcome functionality page downloads the channel catalog by itself instead of leaving the toggle on with an empty channel list. Turning the row off during the download cancels it, and revisiting the page with a catalog already stored downloads nothing.

name: Home Favourites Section
description: Watch home screen always offers Favourites as its last section, before Settings, listing marks from the watch itself and from registered network resources

name: Wear OS home sections and view modes
description: The watch home screen opens with a row reserved for the resources opened most recently - one cell per column, so two in a two column grid and three in a three column grid - and the predefined sections Resources, Phone, Local, Streams, Apps and Favourites always begin at the first cell of the row below it, whether or not any resource has been opened. Missing shortcuts leave empty cells that are not tap targets, a repeat opening moves a resource to the front rather than listing it twice, and a single column list draws the shortcuts as ordinary chips with no reserved gap. View mode is one stored value shared with the Resources page, Settings sits in a command bar under the content, the three watch players hold the screen on while playing or viewing, and every other watch screen follows a keep-awake setting.

name: Selective resource transfer to the watch
description: The phone picks which registered resources travel to the watch on a full-screen picker reached from Wear Companion; an empty selection sends nothing and says so instead of pushing the whole registry.

name: File grid view with thumbnails on the watch
description: The watch file lists for a registered network resource and for local watch media can be shown as a list or as a grid of two or three columns. Grid cells carry a real picture: the watch reads only the head of a network file to take the preview the camera embedded there. A file with no obtainable preview keeps its type icon. The column count falls back from three to two wherever three would give a target under 48 dp. The view is a separate stored setting from the navigation screens one.

name: Grid view with thumbnails for the paired phone folders
description: The paired phone folders listed on the watch follow the same list-or-grid view as the watch own file lists, and the phone prepares each cell picture for its folders and sends it with the page.

name: Saved photo matches the viewfinder
description: The photo the in-app camera saves is the frame the viewfinder showed at the shutter press, for every frame shape and at zoom past the lens optical maximum, where the preview used to keep more of the scene than the file did.

name: Open a stream on the watch
description: A channel menu on the phone can start a stream playing on the paired watch: the watch stores the channel and, when its app is on screen, opens the matching player. When the watch app is closed the phone says so plainly instead of claiming playback, because the platform does not allow waking it from a Data Layer message.

name: Rotation keeps the standalone player surface
description: Standalone player: the video picture and the audio controls survive a screen rotation when the file was opened from another app

name: Long-press actions on calculator keys
description: Holding a calculator key runs a second action shown in small type under the key's own symbol: digits carry the functions by mnemonic (1 is 1/x, 2 is x squared, and so on), operators carry the menu rows (copy, paste, share, round, save history), and holding zero types three zeros. Clearing the history stays menu-only, so it is never one held finger away. A pinch steps the history text through five sizes and remembers the choice, and holding the menu key leaves the calculator. The watch calculator gets three of these: three zeros, leaving by the menu key, and history sizing stepped by the crown.

name: Calculator Operation Element and Function Grid
description: Watch calculator shows the operation beside the value and repeats it on a tap; its function menu is laid out in columns

name: Settings Search Jump Opens The Target Section
description: Settings search jump expands the collapsible section holding the target row on every settings tab

name: Mini-programs section on the watch
description: Watch home screen carries an Apps section holding a calculator, a network monitor of the watch own radios and a mini-game, each usable with the phone out of range

name: Rectangular grid cells across the watch
description: Every grid on the watch - files, streams, resources, home sections and mini-programs - draws rectangular cells: a thumbnail fills its cell with no plate underneath it, and an item without a thumbnail shows its type glyph inside a thin frame.

name: Paired watch as a media resource
description: Add the paired watch as a resource alongside local and cloud ones: browse what it holds, copy or move files onto it from any phone screen, and receive files the watch sends back into your chosen destination. Transfers are capped at 32 MB per file and report their outcome through the usual transfer notification.

name: Active sensor area per camera in System info
description: The System info report names each camera's and each physical sub-lens's active sensor rectangle, so a report pasted back carries the frame that crop calculations are expressed against

name: Host Ping Probe
description: Ping probe against target host with mechanism and status feedback

name: Hop-by-hop Traceroute
description: Traceroute path ladder walking with TTL bounds and silent hop support

name: Resource Speed Test
description: Dedicated speed test section with read/write throughput and read-only indicator

name: Active camera selector icon
description: Update camera switch button icon to visually reflect active lens (front/macro/ultrawide/tele/wide)

name: Camera shooting modes and Document profile
description: Add Document camera shooting mode, display icons in mode selection menu, and fix menu item order/stability

name: Tap to focus and exposure metering
description: Tap-to-focus auto-focus and auto-exposure metering with precise visual focus ring positioning

name: Wear OS Web Portal & In-App Link
description: Public multi-language web portal for Wear OS features with screenshots, store links, and in-app entrances from phone and watch.

name: Launcher Web Portal & In-App Link
description: Public multi-language web portal for Launcher Desktop Mode with car tablet walkthroughs, screenshots, and in-app entrances.

name: Remembered video frame mode
description: The watch video player's frame-mode button - fit against crop-and-pan - now remembers the choice: it survives leaving the player and restarting the app, and one memory covers both a file and a stream, since both open the same player. A watch that has never touched the button still fits the frame.

name: Close the app from the watch home screen
description: The watch home screen's bottom command row now carries a Close button beside Settings: it ends the app outright and drops its task, so the next launch starts at the home screen instead of returning to wherever the user left off.

name: Pin a stream on the watch
description: Mark a stream from the watch video player with the same star that marks a file, and marked channels are listed first on the streams screen. The mark is keyed by the channel address, so it survives a catalogue re-import, and it is kept in the existing watch favourites store rather than a second one.

name: Multi-column settings layout
description: Watch settings screens lay their controls out in rows of two or three where the display width allows it, using the same column-fit rule as the content lists: a control whose label needs the whole width keeps it, and no control shrinks below the tap threshold

name: Voice recorder with playback, file operations and transfer to the phone
description: Record a voice note on the watch, listen to it there, operate on it as a file, and have it land in a phone destination. Recording is held by a foreground service, so it survives the screen going dark and the wrist dropping, and while a recording runs the status dot and the elapsed counter carry their own tone so the state is visible at a glance. A finished note can be played on the watch straight from the recorder screen or from any row of the note list, in the watch's own audio player. A note is published into the watch's shared audio collection carrying a readable title built from the time it was recorded, so it appears among the other audio files as a named recording rather than a filename stamp. A long press on a note opens the same file-actions menu an ordinary watch file gets, so a note can be renamed - which is what tells two notes apart when both are named after the second they were recorded in - as well as sent and deleted. Renaming moves both halves of a published note, its private file and its row in the shared collection, or neither. The local group has its own entry into the voice notes, beside the folder-browse button. Notes are kept on the watch until deleted by hand, and a setting chooses between sending each finished note to the phone automatically or keeping notes until sent by hand. A note taken while the phone is out of reach is listed as waiting and leaves on its own when the link returns.

name: Pinned streams toolbar
description: The search/filter/sort toolbar on the watch streams screen stays pinned at the top of the screen while the channel list scrolls, instead of scrolling away with it; the list reserves space so the first channel is never hidden behind it.

name: Branded first frame on cold start
description: Watch app shows a real Fast Media Sorter wordmark full screen for a moment on cold start, since the system splash cannot render text at watch size

name: Open on the watch even when the watch app is closed
description: Send a stream from the phone to a watch whose screen is dark and the watch now says so: it raises a notification naming what arrived, and one tap opens it straight in the player. Before this the channel was saved silently and nothing was visible until the watch app was opened by hand. When the watch app is already on screen nothing changes - the player opens at once and no notification appears - and a notification is cleared both by the tap and by opening the app, so a stale command never sits in the watch's shade. The watch asks for notification permission once, at the moment a command arrives while the app is open; refusing it simply keeps the previous behaviour and is never asked again.

name: Send a photo, video or track straight to your watch
description: The Send to.. menu now lists your paired watch. Pick it and the photo, GIF, video or track you have open on the phone opens on the watch itself, with no need to go looking for the same file on the small screen. A file kept on a network or cloud source is downloaded first, with progress you can cancel by going back. The watch app has to be open for the file to appear, and the phone tells you exactly which of the six things happened - opened, the watch is not reachable, the watch did not answer, the watch app is closed, the watch cannot show that type, or the file is above the 32 MB the watch accepts. Documents, text and EPUB never offer the watch at all.

name: Wear OS Tiles
description: Wear OS tiles for quick access to assigned network resources, audio/video streams, and favorites list.

name: Calculator keypad and value legibility
description: The watch calculator reads at a glance: the keypad opens on its first row with every key drawn and pressed at the full 48 dp target instead of shrinking away from the screen centre, the subtraction key draws a full-width minus sign rather than a short hyphen, the low-ink glyphs are one type step larger than the digits, clear and backspace sit on a red plate so neither is mistaken for arithmetic, and the running value is right-aligned in its own color like a calculator register.

name: Network Monitor asks for the permissions it reads
description: The Network Monitor's permission notice is now the control that requests them: the watch declares NEARBY_WIFI_DEVICES and BLUETOOTH_CONNECT and the sampling reads both, but nothing ever asked for them, so the Bluetooth page and the visible-Wi-Fi row read unavailable on every watch above API 31. Tapping the notice raises the system request; the fields recover on the next reading.

name: Watch game levels get harder and are shown
description: The watch mini-game now scales with the level: the enemy count rises in steps up to a cap and the difficulty band advances with it, and the level reached is drawn in the header beside the turn count. The board generator is untouched, so a level config and its seed still produce the same board on the phone and the watch.

name: Watch game board is drawn whole on a round display
description: The game board is capped by the largest square the display shape admits and by the height left under the header. Before this it took the full content width, which on a round watch put all four corners outside the glass, and pushed the level-finished button off the bottom of the screen.

name: System information moved to Applications as a two-column report
description: The watch's system-information report is reached from Applications rather than from Settings, where it configured nothing, and its five sections now pack two fields per row instead of one per full-width row. A field too wide for half the screen keeps a row of its own.

name: Desktop shortcut icons top-aligned
description: Launcher desktop shortcut cells align their icon to the cell's top edge instead of centering it, so a row mixing 1-line and 2-line shortcut labels keeps every icon at the same vertical offset.

name: Installed-app import lands in its own Desktop section
description: Importing the installed applications from launcher settings creates a single Desktop section and fills it alphabetically, growing that section when it runs out of room instead of scattering shortcuts through the widget, resource and other sections that still had gaps; running the import again refills the same section rather than adding a second header. The action is named 'Import all installed apps', which is what it does - the home-screen layout of a previously used launcher is not readable by any app.

name: App functions default entries
description: Fresh install or launcher reset now seeds the App functions section with all 11 toggleable programs (Streams, Quick Camera, Quick Voice, Calculator, Network Monitor, Camera OCR, Screen Recording, Link Download, Game, System Information, Wear Companion), matching the Programs and scenarios panel.

name: Stream shortcut picker responsiveness
description: Picking a channel for a launcher shortcut or a stream widget no longer waits on the whole catalog: icons are cut only for the rows shown, the catalog is read once per burst of picks, a large catalog asks for a search term or a topic first, and an empty result says so instead of leaving the loading label on screen

name: Stream window desktop cell
description: Bind one internet channel to its own launcher desktop cell, chosen when the cell is added: a radio channel shows its name, icon and a play/pause button, a video channel shows a larger cell (3x2) with the stream playing inside it that pauses on the last frame. Nothing starts playing until the user presses play.

name: World clock desktop gadget
description: Show the time in another time zone on the launcher desktop, next to the local clock rather than instead of it. The zone is picked from a searchable list of every zone the device knows when the cell is added, and the cell is captioned with the city and how far ahead or behind local time it is. A long press on a placed cell changes its zone.

name: File actions on the watch, with the paired phone as recipient
description: Long press a file in the watch browser to start selecting, tap to add more or use select all, then send the selection to the paired phone, move it there, delete it, or rename it. Delete and rename apply only to files the app itself keeps on the watch; MediaStore items can be sent but not edited, and files browsed over SMB, FTP or SFTP are read-only. A move removes the watch copy only after the phone confirms the transfer, and a name conflict is resolved by auto-renaming with the final name shown in the per-file result.

name: Watch app background chosen from the phone
description: The Wear companion opens as a full window of collapsible setting groups instead of one bottom sheet, and a new group picks what the watch draws behind its screens: the branded waves-and-particles animation, or an image of your own. A picked image is cropped and scaled to the watch frame on the phone and sent over the file channel, and the window reports whether it reached the watch.

name: Wear home navigation and visual system
description: The watch home screen drops the app-name header and opens centred on the first navigation tile, the saved view mode now shapes the two category screens as well as home, placeholder glyphs fill their cell without a frame, and every content type is drawn from one icon set with one semantic palette.

name: The watch Network Monitor draws its pages
description: Every page of the watch Network Monitor now shows its section title, its readings and the permission notice. The page indicator, which spans the whole screen by design, had been sitting inside the content column and taking all of its height, so the pager beside it was measured at zero and drew nothing at all - the program had been blank since it shipped.

name: Location explained by what the build actually does
description: The location entry in the permissions list names every use this build has for it - writing coordinates into the photos and videos you shoot and, on builds that ship them, the desktop compass, speed, altitude and map gadgets and the network monitor's GNSS and Wi-Fi sections. A build without those surfaces keeps the shorter geotag-only wording.

name: Image translation plate opaque backing
description: The translation plate drawn over OCR-detected text in the image overlay is fully opaque, so the original source text no longer shows through underneath the translated text.

name: One colour per content type across every screen
description: A content type now carries the same colour wherever the app colours it - the statistics distribution chart, the media-type badges on each row of the Resources list, and the resource icons. Previously each of those screens kept its own colour table, so the same type could appear in three different hues and one hue could stand for two different types. Every colour now has a matching dark-theme variant, and the thumbnail placeholder no longer tints itself by type.

name: Media library item layout on the watch
description: A media library item on the watch tells itself apart at a glance: the grid caption shows the file name on two lines instead of truncating it after one, a missing thumbnail is replaced by a content-type glyph filling the whole cell rather than a small emoji, and each list row carries its own coloured type icon beside the name instead of a character glued to the detail line.

name: Network Monitor History logs transitions, not repeats
description: The watch Network Monitor's History page now records a row only when the active transport changes, and each row shows the transition's own clock time above the transport name. A session that stays on one network produces one row instead of up to twenty identical copies of the same reading.

name: Open a file you found on the watch on your phone instead
description: A file the paired phone holds can be handed back to the phone for a proper look at it. In the watch's phone browser, tap a file the watch cannot show - a PDF, a text file, an archive - or long press any file, and pick Open on phone: if the phone app is already on screen the file opens there at once, and if it is not, the phone raises a notification naming the file, and one tap opens it in the right viewer. Nothing has to be copied to the watch first, so the offer is there on the very first tap instead of after a wait, and a file the watch has no player for is never fetched at all. When the phone cannot show anything because its notifications are switched off, the watch says exactly that rather than going quiet, so the fix is on the phone and not a guess about range.

name: Start and stop a slideshow from the watch image viewer
description: Start or stop a picture slideshow with a command on the viewing screen itself, instead of only from settings. Turning the slideshow setting off now also stops a show that is already running on an open screen.

name: Choose how a picture fits the watch display
description: Switch a picture between fitting the whole frame and filling the screen, with a command on the viewer. The choice is remembered and comes back the next time a picture is opened, matching what the watch video player already offers.

name: Wear Companion controls announce themselves
description: Every control in the Wear Companion window carries a name for accessibility services: each media-type switch reads as its own label with its state, the two view-mode rows name which mode they set, and the background options, the slideshow interval and every action button announce what they do.

name: Keep the watch screen on across every screen
description: With the watch Keep screen on setting enabled, the display stays awake on every screen of the watch app, the startup splash and the permission screen included, not only after the main navigation is reached. Screen-on requests are counted, so leaving a player for an ordinary screen no longer drops the setting's own hold, and with the setting off the audio, video and image players keep their existing behaviour.

name: Watch file remote destination
description: Saves files received from the watch to configured network or cloud destinations with notification reporting

name: Wear OS complication data sources
description: Watch face complications for last used resource, favourites count and now playing track with automatic ambient rendering and event-driven updates.

name: Receive file outcome ack and destination on watch
description: Sending a file from watch to phone now reports whether the file landed in a local folder or was queued for upload on the phone, naming the destination. If a background upload fails later, the watch receives a notification.

name: Add-flow target square survives process death
description: Launcher add-flow no longer drops the picked cell to (0,0) when the OS kills the process mid-flow (e.g. system contact/app/resource picker) - the target square now survives via SavedStateHandle.

name: Add or open the watch resource from the companion window
description: The Wear companion window carries a button that turns the paired watch into a resource on the first tap and opens it in the browser on every later one, so the watch reaches the file lists and the destination picker without walking through the add-resource wizard. There is one watch row by construction - a second tap never creates a duplicate.

name: Two-way Wear OS settings sync
description: Every watch setting can be changed on the watch or in the phone companion window, and one Sync settings button on either side brings both to the same state, keeping whichever side changed each field later. Two settings stay watch-only by design (auto rotation, voice note delivery) and the background picture stays a phone choice. Both sides show when they last agreed.

name: Live camera desktop wallpaper
description: The launcher desktop wallpaper can be a live frame from one of the device cameras, with the lens chosen from a list when the mode is picked. The entry is offered only on devices that report a camera, the camera permission is requested on selection, and the stream is released whenever the desktop leaves the screen; a missing camera or a refused permission falls back to the branded wallpaper.

name: Toggle row canonical pattern + descriptions
description: Align Wear Companion toggle rows with the app-wide canonical switch-row pattern (switch left, title, description, optional tooltip button) and add a per-setting watch-impact description plus tooltips for the album-art and keep-awake toggles

name: Per-instance widgets on the launcher desktop
description: The random photo frame and the camera quick capture can be placed on the launcher desktop, completing the home-screen widget bridge at 14 of 14. Adding either cell opens that widget's own configuration screen first, and the cell is placed only once the configuration is confirmed; a cancelled configuration places nothing and leaves no stored instance behind. A desktop cell and the same widget on the system home screen keep separate configurations, because the cell carries a launcher-minted instance token that the platform's own widget ids can never collide with. Removing a configured cell clears its stored instance.

name: Video player volume on the rotary bezel, seeking on a long press
description: On the watch, turning the bezel in the video player now changes media volume instead of moving the playback position, matching the audio player and the platform media convention. Seeking moved to a long press on the previous and next buttons in both players, and those two buttons now stay on screen even for a single file or a stream, so seeking is reachable without a browsed set. TalkBack announces each long press by name.

name: Volume readout in the video player control panel
description: The watch video player shows the current media volume inside its control panel while the panel is visible. Turning the bezel raises the panel if it was hidden, so the level is on screen at the moment it changes and the user is never adjusting volume blind.

name: Current volume shown on the watch file list
description: The watch file list shows the current media volume as a small bar above the files, so the user can see how loud the next file will be before tapping it. The bar is read-only and reads the level once when the screen opens; volume is still changed from the player bezel or the watch buttons.

name: Search, filter and sort inside a resource
description: Every watch screen that lists the contents of a resource carries a search, filter and sort row above the list, on all four content routes. Search matches part of the file name and takes keyboard or voice; the filter narrows by content type and appears only when the list actually holds more than one; sort offers the source order plus name, date and size both ways. The phone-folder route offers five orders rather than seven, because the watch is never sent a date for those entries. Narrowing is recomputed in memory and never re-reads the source, and a list emptied by it says nothing matched rather than reading as an empty resource. Without a phone the watch refines its local categories and network sources on its own; the phone-category and phone-folder routes need the phone connected, as they do to list anything at all. The choices last for the visit and are not remembered.

name: Picture-in-picture from every host
description: Picture-in-picture now works for streams and videos opened from the launcher home screen, restores the player chrome exactly as it was when PiP ends, and says so on screen when a device refuses it.

name: Standalone picture-in-picture keeps its video frame
description: The picture-in-picture window opened from an externally launched video now shows the video instead of a black rectangle.

name: The name is written on the icon when the icon says nothing
description: A file drawn with the shared type tile - a document, a sound file, an archive - now carries its own name written across that tile, over as many lines as the tile holds. Two files whose names begin the same way no longer look identical. On the watch the name is white with a black outline and nothing is drawn behind it, so the tile stays fully visible between the letters; the same applies to channels, network sources, favourites and any item still waiting for its picture. Anything showing a real preview is unchanged.

name: Dialog action pair named button styles
description: Extensions manager footer and camera lens picker dialog now use the named Button Taxonomy family (Filled/Destructive/DialogConfirm/DialogCancel) instead of raw Material3 styles, and the dark theme regained the materialAlertDialogTheme seam it was missing

name: Calculator settings and layout modes
description: Calculator settings for thousands separator, result font size and keypad layout modes, with copy-by-tap on result and selectable history

name: Phone Live Search
description: Phone Browse live search box in command bar with instant in-memory filtering

name: Calm message for unreachable media
description: A media file that fails to open because its network resource is unreachable now shows a calm dialog naming the cause, with Retry, instead of a critical program error. A file the server reports as missing is named separately as gone and can be removed from favorites in one tap; an unreachable resource never offers removal.

name: One confirmation for copied text
description: Copying text anywhere in the app now shows a single, consistently worded confirmation instead of six different messages across thirteen places. On Android 13 and later no toast is shown at all, because the system displays its own clipboard preview and a second message would stack over the same action.

name: Network Monitor external IP and system settings integration
description: Displays external IP and copy button on Network Monitor summary, opens Android system settings from section headings, and routes launcher signal indicators to Monitor sections.

name: Filter by paired-watch resource type
description: Resource filter dialog can now filter by the paired-watch resource type

name: One content-type vocabulary across every watch source
description: Every source on the watch - its own storage, the paired phone and a network share - offers its categories from one place, so a category means the same thing and is named and coloured the same wherever it appears. Documents are among them, the images category is called Images on every screen, All opens a flat list of media files with no folders, and Browse walks the folders of the source with all of its files. A source that cannot serve a category does not show it, and the rule that decides is stated once.

name: An empty phone category says why it is empty
description: When a category on the paired phone opens with nothing in it, the watch distinguishes two causes. A reachable folder that currently holds no files reads as empty; a category no configured phone resource is set up to hold says so instead, and offers no retry because retrying cannot change the answer. The phone decides which of the two it is, since only the phone sees the resource list and the types each resource is configured to carry.

name: Browse filter no longer bleeds between resources
description: The date/size/media-type filter set in one resource used to reappear when opening a different resource, because it was stored under one app-wide key. It now persists per resource, the same scope as sort order and display mode.

name: The resource list keeps its filter and sort between sessions
description: The sort order and the type, media-type and name filters chosen on the resource list are remembered and reapplied the next time the app opens, including after the app is force-stopped or the device restarts. The filters banner above the list keeps saying which filters are on, so a restored narrow filter reads as filtered rather than as a lost list.

name: The watch browse list keeps its type filter and sort order
description: The content-type filter and the sort order chosen while browsing on the watch are remembered and reapplied on the next visit, including after a restart. A typed search is deliberately not restored, because a query nobody can see would silently empty the list. A remembered type that the opened category does not contain is ignored rather than applied, so remembering a choice can never produce an empty screen, and the filter and sort icons stay highlighted while a restored choice is in force.

name: Folder walk over the watch's own storage
description: The watch's own storage now offers a Browse entry beside its six flat lists, opening a folder walk one level at a time. It covers the app's own file tree, including copies received from the phone that MediaStore never indexes, and reconstructs a hierarchy of shared storage by grouping media entries on their relative path.

name: Gadget failure isolation
description: A failed launcher gadget now leaves the rest of the desktop usable and identifies the affected cell.

name: Status area network indicators
description: Wi-Fi generation digit, Bluetooth connected device count, SIM roaming and data type, and transfer speed readouts in the launcher taskbar status strip

name: Weather place survives a launcher reset
description: The city picked for a desktop weather block is remembered outside the desktop itself, so resetting the launcher to defaults brings the block back already showing that city instead of an empty one asking to pick again

name: Launcher back navigation return
description: Return Launcher-started targets to Launcher on Back

name: Front flashlight reachable everywhere the other programs are
description: The front flashlight is now a full internal program: it appears in the programs menu and the programs panel beside the calculator and the network monitor, and it can be placed on the Android home screen as its own one-cell widget. One tap on the widget lights the screen, one touch of the lit screen closes it - there is nothing else to configure. All of it stays behind the existing flashlight switch in settings, so turning that switch off removes the menu item and hides the widget from the picker.

name: Launcher reset widget instance cleanup
description: Launcher reset now clears stored instances of configured widget cells instead of leaving unreachable data behind

name: Configurable desktop swipe actions
description: Assign any gesture action to each of the four launcher desktop swipes - up, down, left and right - from the same grouped picker the edge gestures use, and set or clear the target app or web address for the actions that take one; defaults open All apps upward and the notification shade downward.

name: YouTube Web Frame Widgets
description: YouTube and YouTube Music embedded web frame widgets

name: Interactive Google Maps live frame
description: Interactive Google Maps live frame widget on Launcher desktop

name: Canonical localized filter facets
description: Stream filter facet values are normalized to canonical ids (category, topic, language, country) and shown as localized readable labels with flags; aliases and typos fold into one filter option and unknown values stay visible.

name: Widget backdrop opacity persistence
description: Launcher widget backdrop opacity now persists across process restarts: the launcher settings store reads and writes the float, a missing key keeps the 0.85 default, and launcher reset still restores it.

name: Idle dimming and blackout
description: Add launcher idle dimming 4s before screen blackout

name: Wear OS file list row icons and on-demand thumbnails
description: Distinguishes Wear OS file list rows with content type icons, synced resource glyphs, and per-row on-demand phone image thumbnails.

name: Offline translator cell on the desktop
description: Translator desktop cell now takes its language pair from the app translation settings, shows it on a caption button that opens those settings, and keeps swap as an in-session override

name: Physical flashlight launcher operation
description: The launcher programs menu, programs panel, and desktop shortcut can toggle the camera physical flash without opening a screen; devices without a flash do not offer the operation, and a temporarily unavailable torch reports a brief retry message.

name: Stream window overlay controls
description: A tap on a playing video channel's desktop window shows auto-hiding corner controls: play/pause, mute, stop, fullscreen, and picture-in-picture. Fullscreen and PiP open the stream in the fullscreen player, which collapses into a PiP window on request.

name: Add window to desktop menu action
description: The channel menu on the launcher desktop gains Add window to desktop, which places the channel's stream window in the first free desktop slot in one step and reports success or no-space by toast.

name: Persistent audio by default
description: Audio channels keep playing after the screen turns off: persistent audio playback is enabled by default and stays switchable in settings.

name: Desktop lock double tap
description: Double tap on empty launcher desktop space switches the existing desktop edit lock; enabled by default with a toggle row in launcher settings.

name: All apps alphabetical groups
description: All Apps now has an expandable preview and alphabetical groups.

name: Shared surface transparency
description: Use one launcher backdrop transparency setting for widgets, labels, section headers, and the Start panel.

name: Open All apps from an edge gesture
description: Assign the launcher's All apps list to an edge-gesture slot; the gesture brings the home screen forward with the list already open, reusing the running desktop rather than starting a second copy.

name: Clock display gestures
description: The Clock desktop gadget supports directional swipes: hide or restore seconds, choose a random readable dial colour and a new time typeface, or restore the theme colour. The selected seconds visibility, dial colour and time typeface persist across launcher restarts; the date keeps its typeface while sharing the dial colour.

name: Double tap the desktop to lock the screen
description: A double tap on empty desktop space locks the device screen. Where the device lock is out of reach, the launcher blacks the screen out with its own full-screen overlay instead, and any tap or key brings the desktop back. The gesture can be switched off in the launcher settings.

name: Edit and clear the address of an edge-gesture slot
description: The target of an edge-gesture slot - the app it launches or the web address it opens - is shown as its own row under the assigned action, so it can be re-read, corrected and cleared at any time. Previously only the app target had such a row: an address was asked for once, right after the action was picked, and was unreachable afterwards.

name: Readable section titles
description: Launcher section titles remain readable over light wallpapers.

name: Recent taskbar context actions
description: Long-press a recent taskbar shortcut to open it, pin it to the taskbar, or remove it from recent history.

name: Screen paging gesture and move to another screen
description: Assign next-screen or previous-screen paging to any desktop swipe, and in edit mode tap an object to move it - or a whole group - to another screen.

name: Configurable All apps swipe actions
description: Assign one of five actions to each of the four swipes on the launcher All apps panel - back to the desktop, expand the full app list instead of the alphabetical sections, launch a chosen app, lock the screen, or leave the direction unused - from the same grouped picker the other gesture surfaces use. Swiping down at the top of the list returns to the desktop and swiping up at its end expands the full list by default; screen lock is offered only in builds that can perform it.

name: Starter desktop composed for the device profile and screen class
description: The seeded launcher desktop now picks its section order, per-section item count and screen count from the device profile together with the screen size and aspect ratio, instead of one hardcoded two-screen layout.

name: Welcome first page pitches the app by its roles
description: The first page of the setup wizard introduces the app through role tiles. A build that ships the launcher leads with the home-screen role and invites you to make the app your home screen; streams and the Wear OS watch app each get their own tile where the build has them, instead of hiding inside the More tile; and the one-tap Enable all shortcut carries the green confirm fill.

name: Enable all explains the system screens before it starts
description: Tapping Enable all on the welcome screen first shows what will happen: the Android permission requests, the settings pages left with Back, and the Open with sheet raised over one of the user's own files where FastMediaSorter must be picked with Always. Small letter-free pictures show where to tap. A second reminder appears immediately before the default-app stage, and declining either one leaves the corresponding step unrun.

name: Value stays next to the caption it belongs to
description: The value now sits immediately after the caption that names it in the network monitor rows, the statistics metric and legend rows, the camera and slideshow dialogs and the scheduled tasks widget row, instead of travelling to the far edge of a wide or landscape screen.

name: Pick the messenger before the contact
description: Pinning a Message in App cell now asks which messaging app the chat should open in first, then opens the contact picker and keeps only that app's channels for the person picked. The list is discovered from the apps installed on the device and needs no contacts permission to build. An 'Any app' row keeps the original order, where the contact is chosen first and the app afterwards, and the question is skipped entirely when fewer than two messengers are installed. If the person turns out to have no chat in the chosen app, the message says which app that was.

name: Watch splash shows the app icon
description: The watch cold-start splash shows the app launcher icon on a black background, drawn by the platform itself, instead of the brand arrows glyph it carried before. Google Play's Wear app quality rule WO-V15 requires the splash icon to match the launcher icon, and the branded glyph did not - the watch submission was rejected for it. The branded first frame that follows the splash now shows the same launcher icon, so both startup surfaces carry one mark.

name: Phone-pinned streams lead the watch list
description: Streams pinned on the phone are raised into the top group of the watch's streams list, next to the marks made on the watch itself, so the two or three channels actually watched are reachable without scrolling a catalogue of many thousands of rows. The phone republishes the whole pinned set whenever it changes, so unpinning on the phone withdraws the channel from the watch's top group while a mark placed on the watch stays. A channel is matched by identity rather than by raw address, so the phone and the watch catalogue spelling one address with different http and https schemes still refer to the same channel.
