Requires the Wear companion.

name: Readable stream filter and most-used ordering on the watch
description: On the watch, the stream filter names topics and languages in the interface language instead of raw catalog English, and lists them most-populated first with the channel count on each row, with the app's own three languages on top. The sort dialog offers Most used, Name A-Z, Name Z-A and By media type; Most used is the default and rises with the channels actually started on the watch. The chosen filter and sort survive leaving the screen, restarting the app and rebooting the watch.

name: Copy the watch calculator result
description: A tap on the watch calculator result puts it on the watch clipboard, so it can be pasted into a messenger or any other app on the wrist without going through the phone. Watches below Android 13 get their own on-screen confirmation, and where the system already draws one it is not repeated. A tap does nothing while the display carries an error.

name: Voice notes survive a watch database failure
description: When the watch cannot open its voice-note database - a schema change no migration covers, or a corrupt file - the watch app no longer dies moments after launch. The store is recreated and its index is rebuilt from the recordings still on disk, so the note list returns with the same files, dates and durations; a recording that cannot be read for its length is still listed rather than dropped. Every recovered note waits for a manual send instead of queueing itself, so nothing reaches the phone twice, and the note list explains once that it was rebuilt and that sending status was reset.

name: Shortcut sync for tools enabled after seeding
description: A tool switched on after the launcher desktop was already laid out receives its own desktop cell in both orientations, without a restart and without leaving launcher mode. Only newly enabled routes are added: an existing desktop is left untouched at update time, a cell deleted by hand is not restored, and switching a tool off keeps its cell.

name: Companion
description: Gate Wear companion outbound Data Layer calls and stream pins publisher on enableWearCompanion setting

name: Honest disclosure for permission-limited folders
description: A folder connected by file path on a build that cannot read shared storage whole says so on screen: the browse list carries a persistent line naming what can be read through it, the filter dialog stops offering document types the folder cannot return, and the resource tile qualifies its count instead of presenting a partial listing as complete. Where nothing readable remains, as on the All documents aggregate, the tile says so in words rather than showing a zero. Where the Reconnect resource action exists, the line names it rather than sending the user to re-add the folder and lose its favorites and schedules. Compiled into every flavor; the disclosure appears from API 30 wherever all-files access is not held - a build that never declares the permission, or one that declares it and has not been granted it

name: Reconnect a direct-path folder through the system chooser
description: Reconnect a direct-path folder resource through the system folder picker, preserving the resource's settings, favorites, schedules and quick-sort destination. Compiled into every flavor; the menu entry appears only where the direct file route is unobtainable - API 30+ on a build that does not declare all-files access

name: SAF Resource Quick Verify
description: Fix SAF resource file list emptying after returning from viewer twice

name: Reconnect Mismatch Dialog Recreation
description: Fix reconnect mismatch dialog disappearing on screen recreation

name: Wear Grid Scaling Alignment
description: Pass WearGridScalingParams to 9 ScalingLazyColumn surfaces on Wear OS for round display edge clearance

name: Watch mini-game: full-size board, counters around it, in-play menu
description: On the watch the mini-game board now fills the largest square the display can draw whole, with the score, level and turn count moved out of two header lines into the band around it; a finished level starts the next one by itself after a short pause, and a long press on the board opens a menu offering skip turn, restart level and exit.

name: Multi-module Room migration upgrade safety
description: Extends Room upgrade safety gates to cover all Room databases including watch and adds gating migration execution step to wear pre-release sweep.

name: Wear Network Monitor revision and navigation
description: Opens on a summary dashboard carrying the active link with the local and external address, and a button panel whose every section shows a live fact. Each section is its own destination reached by tap and left by the platform edge swipe: Wi-Fi with frequency, standard and a restartable signal trend; mobile, which explains itself on a watch with no modem; Bluetooth; satellites listed by constellation with coordinates, accuracy and fix time; traffic rates with resettable counters; internet with an on-demand reachability check; and the session history. Addresses copy to the clipboard and each section opens its own system settings screen.

name: Watch system information reports what no watch settings screen shows
description: The watch's system-information report now answers why the watch or the app is misbehaving instead of repeating the watch's own settings. It adds thermal state, battery temperature, voltage and remaining charge in mAh, uptime, boot count, battery-optimisation exemption, background restriction and the reason the app's process last died; the sensor inventory with each sensor's vendor, power draw and resolution; chipset, instruction sets, core count and low-memory flag; and the supported Wi-Fi bands and standards. The phone link stops being a yes/no and names each connected device, whether it is nearby or reached through the cloud, its node id, this watch's own node id and the capability set of the pair. Storage now measures the app's own data, cache and cache reserve rather than the whole partition. Long lists collapse to a count and open on tap, and a Refresh button re-reads the facts that change while the screen is open. A section this watch cannot fill says why instead of disappearing.

name: Delete, rename and move a file the watch itself holds
description: A photo taken on the watch or a voice note recorded there used to offer one action only, sending it to the phone. The long-press menu now offers delete, rename and move for it too. Each write asks the system to confirm first, because the file belongs to the watch's own shared storage rather than to the app, and the operation finishes on that answer rather than failing silently. Where the platform offers no confirmation dialog at all the operation is not listed, so the menu never proposes something that would end in a refusal. Both menus, the one for a selection and the one for a single file, show the same set. Files opened over SMB, FTP or SFTP stay read-only.

name: Send to.. on the watch
description: The file menu on the watch opens the same Send to.. list the phone offers - email, messengers, printing, the clipboard, the system share - as its first entry, above sending to the phone. The list is declared once on the phone and published to the watch, so a receiver switched off in the phone's settings is absent on the watch and one added later appears there without a second list to keep in step. A receiver the watch can serve itself runs on the watch with no phone nearby. One it cannot is marked 'via phone' and keeps its place in the list even while the phone is out of reach, which is said before the transfer starts rather than as a failure at the end. When the phone serves it, the file crosses the bridge and the phone offers it as a notification action; the watch reports that it is waiting for a tap on the phone, and never claims an external app already took it. A receiver that does not exist on this watch is absent rather than dimmed.

name: Lock the desktop from the desktop
description: A long press on empty space on the launcher desktop offers 'Lock changes', which freezes the layout without a trip to settings; a long press on an already locked desktop answers with a toast naming the lock and where to lift it, instead of doing nothing.

name: Stereo balance presets
description: Stereo-balance presets (50/50, 30/70, 70/30) in the shared playback-control dialog, applied through a new channel-balance audio processor to every playback path including background audio and standalone video

name: Background audio playback service
description: Audio files and streams keep playing on the watch after the app is minimized while they are sounding; pausing releases the foreground service and its notification. Background playback uses an opt-in switch.

name: Installed build identifies itself by its build time
description: Every installable artifact carries the date and time it was built in its version string, so the version shown on the device tells you which build you are running. Applies to any packaging path - a build script, a raw gradle invocation, a CI job or the IDE Run button - and a mechanical gate rejects an artifact whose version does not match its own build.

name: Cloud sources stay signed in after moving to a new device
description: Moving to a new Android device no longer means signing in to your cloud sources again. The app carries the sign-in state over through the system transfer, so the first launch on the new phone already shows Google Drive and Dropbox connected. Signing out beforehand removes the carried state, so a session you left does not come back. Nothing is shown when there is nothing to carry - the ordinary sign-in is offered as usual. OneDrive still needs a manual sign-in, because its library keeps the token where the app cannot read it.

name: Taskbar button context menu
description: Long-press context menu on launcher taskbar buttons allowing launch, pin/unpin and remove actions

name: Standard window header, screen-level sync row and documentation links
description: The Wear companion window carries the app's standard toolbar with a back arrow and safe system-bar insets, shows the sync action with its last-synced status on one row above the collapsible watch settings, sizes every form button to its own label, marks the sync action with the app's watch icon, and ends with a link block to the Wear portal and the watch install guide

name: Last successful sync and the watch build that accepted it
description: The companion window shows when the last full settings exchange with the watch actually completed, and which version of the watch app accepted it. The time moves only when the watch answers with its own settings report, so a press that reached nothing leaves the previous time standing. A watch build that reports no version shows an explicit unknown, and a version differing from the phone's is highlighted.

name: Compact refine overlay and one readable refine menu while browsing
description: While browsing files on the watch the search and refine controls are drawn as small outlined icons with no plate over the list, hide themselves while the list is scrolled and return when it stops; the search icon goes straight to text or voice input, and one refine menu screen carries the sort orders and the content-type filter as one-column lists with full labels, explains in a sentence when a list holds a single type, and is where an active query is shown and cleared

name: Universal back affordance
description: Visible back button on every Wear navigation screen (left edge, vertical middle), close cross vs minimize double-chevron on the home screen by live playback state, back command inside all three player control clusters

name: Wear list top-edge placement
description: Watch lists open with content flush at the top edge instead of below a centering reservation

name: Wear unified toggles
description: Unified watch toggle style with blue/brown state tints, media type category labels and continuous Streams row

name: Content-sized centred wear action button sets
description: Watch action menus present content-sized centred button sets with icons on each entry

name: Wallpaper choices and settings scope
description: Choose an animated or stationary branded wallpaper, or a phone-delivered photo, for Wear navigation screens.

name: Wear Companion Resource Picker & Grouped Settings
description: Wear Companion resource picker groups, default selection rules, and split settings cards

name: Transparent settings icon grid
description: Restyle the Wear settings grid as transparent icon targets

name: Tap zones, self-hiding controls and pinch zoom in the watch image viewer
description: The watch image viewer opens on the picture alone: tap the left or right third to page, tap the middle to show the controls, and they hide themselves after fifteen seconds. Play shows the next picture at once, and a cropped picture can be pinched and dragged.

name: Phone resolves reachable companion SFTP endpoint and sends group
description: Phone resolves active reachable endpoint of companion and passes full address group to watch during sync

name: Web portal links in the watch About section
description: The About section on the watch offers the web portal as two links - one opens the watch's own browser, the other hands the address to the paired phone through the Wear OS companion. Each press reports its outcome on screen instead of failing silently.

name: Watch selects reachable endpoint and names failure cause
description: Watch probes address group before connecting to network source and classifies connection failures into specific user messages

name: Wear calculator clear-button placement
description: Repositioned the Wear calculator clear action below the keypad with a guarded gap and wider result field.

name: Resource edits survive a phone-watch sync
description: A network resource edited on the watch is no longer overwritten by the phone's copy on the next sync, and an edit made on the phone is no longer dropped by the watch's export. Each side records when it last changed a resource, the exchange corrects for the two devices' clock difference, and the side that edited later wins - the same rule the settings sync already used, applied to a resource as a whole. A resource that exists on only one side is still added rather than removed, and a sync with an older phone or watch that sends no edit time behaves exactly as before.

name: Watch mini-game: a random board every time and a start-of-level arrow
description: Every board in the watch mini-game is now drawn from a fresh random seed, so two games in a row differ and restarting a level gives a new board instead of a second try at the same one; a restored save still returns the exact board and position the player left. Each new board opens with a short arrow drawn from the player to the nearest exit, matching the phone, and it fades on its own without any input.

name: Watch streams: a compact list counter and a pin instead of a heart
description: The watch stream list now shows how many channels the current search and filters leave, stacked over the size of the whole catalog in two small lines, so a long total no longer eats the width of the search, filter and sort buttons; it stays hidden while the list is loading, empty or failed. The mark on a playing stream is now a pin rather than a heart, filled when the stream is pinned and outlined when it is not, and TalkBack calls it pinning rather than adding to favourites - the action itself is unchanged and still lifts the stream to the top of the list. A playing stream no longer draws the position counter, which moved to the list where a channel is actually chosen. Favourites for local files, photos and videos are untouched.

name: Last played channel in the watch home recent row
description: The watch home screen's recent row lists the last played stream channel beside recently opened network resources, ordered by one recency; tapping it opens the channel in the player, and the last-resource complication shows it too.

name: Deleting a resource on one device removes it from the other
description: A network resource deleted on the phone now disappears from the watch at the next sync, and one deleted on the watch disappears from the phone, instead of being handed back by whichever side still had it. Each device remembers that it deleted the resource rather than simply forgetting the resource, so a record missing from one side still means 'created only over there, add it' and is added as before. When one side deletes a resource and the other edits it, the later of the two actions wins, using the same clock-difference correction the edit sync already used, so both devices reach the same answer whichever direction the sync runs. A sync with an older phone or watch that sends no deletions behaves exactly as before and never removes anything.

name: Configurable player panel auto-hide delay
description: Configurable delay in seconds (1 to 600, default 15s) before the video player controls panel automatically hides during playback, applied to the main player and Streams video playback.

name: Watch player panel auto-hide delay setting
description: Configurable auto-hide interval for the controls panel in watch video and image players, adjustable directly on the watch or from the paired phone via Wear companion settings.

name: Taskbar Recents Context Menu
description: Fix taskbar recents long-press context menu unwired

name: Wear Network Monitor Tile Layout
description: Wear Network Monitor summary screen uses rectangular tiles in 1-3 columns based on viewMode setting

name: Equal control-grid layout
description: Align Wear player control buttons into equal four-column rows

name: Wear player play button media color
description: Tint Wear OS player play buttons according to media category icon colors

name: Centered incomplete grid rows
description: Wear grids center incomplete final rows in two- and three-column layouts while preserving full rows, single-column layouts, actions, and accessibility semantics.

name: Watch now-playing home row
description: The watch home screen names what is playing in the background and lets it be stopped or reopened from there, without opening other content.

name: Recent stream shortcut favicon icon
description: Watch home screen: last used stream shortcut displays channel favicon icon

name: Streams initial loading state
description: Wear Streams keeps its loading state until the first catalogue projection completes.

name: Remembered list position on the watch
description: Watch screens reopen on the list item the user left them on

name: Back and skip-turn buttons beside the watch game board
description: The watch mini-game carries the app's standard back arrow at the left middle of the screen and a small skip-turn button opposite it at the right middle, so leaving the game and spending a turn without moving no longer require the long-press menu. The score, level and turn counters moved into one row at the bottom of the ring to free both side positions.

name: Accent theme secondary text color
description: Secondary text color adapts to selected accent theme across all 6 custom color schemes

name: Settings values in a block line up in one column
description: Adjacent caption+value rows on a settings screen or dialog share one caption column sized by the longest caption in the block, so their values start on the same vertical. The column is dropped whenever it would not fit, keeping every value next to its own caption. A row hidden at measure time never sizes the column, and a sub-row belonging to the row above it opts out.

name: Desktop gesture targets
description: Desktop swipe actions may start on shortcuts, section headers and the taskbar while gadgets retain exclusive gesture ownership.

name: Action menu on an App Functions cell
description: Long-pressing a cell in the launcher desktop's App Functions section opens the same popup menu the neighbouring app cell shows: open the feature, open its settings screen where it has one, pin it to the taskbar, or remove the cell from the desktop.

name: Enable all covers every capability the build carries
description: The welcome wizard's Enable all button switches on every setting that unlocks a capability this build ships - the image and GIF media types included, plus each feature route compiled into the flavor - instead of a fixed list of thirteen switches. Privacy, destructive, preference and resource-dependent settings stay untouched.

name: First desktop seed places only launchable features
description: The launcher desktop's first seed places a feature cell only when that feature is both compiled into the build and switched on, so a fresh desktop carries no tile for a capability the user has turned off. A feature enabled later still gets its cell from the reactive shortcut sync, without the desktop being reset.

name: Fresh desktop opens with the cell that names the device
description: The first desktop a profile is seeded with now opens its widget group with one signature cell chosen for that device: a car head unit gets the interactive Google Maps live frame instead of only a Maps icon, and a tablet gets YouTube in its own group rather than only in the row every profile shares. The signature is seeded ahead of everything else the group earns, so a narrow screen trims the rest before it, and an application signature is never seeded twice on one desktop.
